title: The young stars of Taurus
caption: The reflection nebula GN 04.32.8 in the Taurus Molecular Cloud, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: GN 04.32.8, HP Tau · Taurus Molecular Cloud · constellation Taurus · about 480 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: ESA/Hubble Picture of the Week, June 2025 (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: A soft blue cloud glows around three bright stars in this Hubble view. GN 04.32.8 is a reflection nebula: a cloud of dust that makes no light of its own, but scatters the light of nearby stars. Because of how that scattering works, many reflection nebulae, this one included, look blue.

It is a small part of the Taurus Molecular Cloud, a stellar nursery about 480 light-years away and one of the best places to study stars as they form. The star at the very center, V1025 Tauri, does most of the lighting. Another of the three, HP Tauri, is a T Tauri star, a young, energetic, turbulent star early in its life. The trio is believed to be bound together as a triple system.
Just left of center, below the clouds, sits a small, flattened orange spot crossed by a dark line. It is a newborn star hidden behind its disc, which we see edge-on.
scale: Using the source’s listed field of view (2.41 × 2.57 arcminutes) and its distance of about 480 light-years, the frame spans roughly 0.3 × 0.4 light-years. Its light set out about 480 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: Hubble’s cameras through two filters, in visible and near-infrared light. The color assigned to each filter isn’t published.
understand.eye: Ultraviolet and near-infrared light are invisible to the eye, and the colors are assigned, so the eye would not see this palette.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: Edge-on discs like that one are excellent targets: astronomers are using Hubble to study it in detail, hoping to learn what kinds of planets could form in similar discs.
alt: A glowing blue cloud around three bright stars, with a small, flattened orange spot crossed by a dark line just left of center.
